traceability.notes:
All requirements and acceptance criteria for 009.0-DEV-MAINTENANCE-TOOLS appear fully implemented and verified.
Core functionality: detectStaleAnnotations, updateAnnotationReferences, batchUpdateAnnotations, verifyAnnotations, and generateMaintenanceReport together cover detection of stale references, targeted/batch updates, and post-operation verification. Tests exercise both isolated units and end-to-end behavior via the CLI.
Quality and safety: updateAnnotationReferences performs targeted string replacement on @story paths and only writes files when content changes. The maintenance utilities validate directories and skip non-files. Detection logic enforces project boundaries and avoids filesystem access for unsafe or invalid paths. Extensive tests confirm behavior for non-existent roots, permission errors, nested directories, and malformed paths.
Integration and UX: the tools are exposed via src/maintenance, wired to the published binary traceability-maint via package.json, and thoroughly tested through CLI tests that assert exit codes and user-facing output (text and JSON). README provides clear documentation and examples for all commands.
Error handling: CLI commands return distinct exit codes for clean vs stale vs usage/error conditions, validate required flags, support dry-run mode, and handle invalid formats and filesystem errors gracefully. Lower-level detection logic includes safe fallbacks for boundary enforcement failures and file read errors.
Given the concrete implementation, comprehensive test coverage (unit, integration, CLI, and performance), and supporting documentation, this story is assessed as PASSED.
